video.title: The Most Copy-Pastable Online Business (Thanks to AI)

summary: Chris Koerner interviews a Dubai-based builder (name not stated in the transcript) who uses AI coding tools (Cursor, Claude Code) to build programmatic-SEO directory sites. His recipe site Guilty Chef ranks for restaurant-inspired recipes and reportedly gets about 11,000 organic visits a month and about $700-800 a month. His Best Dubai directory ranks near Tripadvisor for restaurant review searches. He demos a scaffold from his own product, 5 Day Sprint, building a protein snacks directory page live, and shows how to duplicate a project to launch more niche sites. The key takeaway is that AI makes niche directory sites cheap to build and clone, but SEO needs patience and the revenue shown is small.

speakers.name: Unnamed guest (Dubai-based builder, designer, agency owner)
speakers.description: Builds AI directory sites Guilty Chef and Best Dubai; sells 5 Day Sprint scaffold and a school community. Name not stated in the transcript.

ideas.name: Guilty Chef - restaurant-inspired recipe programmatic SEO site
ideas.one_liner: AI-generated recipe pages inspired by restaurant dishes, ranking in Google and monetised by a small paid recipe-generator membership.
ideas.business_model: Organic SEO traffic converting to a low-priced paid membership (about $5) for a recipe generator; no ads yet.
ideas.customer: Home cooks searching for copycat recipes of restaurant dishes (for example Wagamama or Wingstop).
ideas.problem: No single aggregated site for restaurant-inspired recipes; existing ones are individual home cooks' blogs.
ideas.offer: Pages of restaurant dishes and recipes, plus a paid section where users generate their own recipes (Anthropic API in the background).

pricing.notes: Speaker says customers 'paid like five bucks or something to join', often at holiday peaks, and many are inactive.

acquisition_channels.details: Programmatic SEO pages per restaurant and dish with schema.org markup, internal links and AI-written content; zero paid ads; rebuilt around June, Google traffic rose from about August 2024. Also surfaces as a source in ChatGPT.

quote.text: I'm spending zero dollars on marketing on this site.
quote.speaker: Guest

ideas.delivery: Content is generated by AI and published as web pages; the paid recipe generator calls Anthropic via API. Built in Webflow with AI components in Cursor.
unit_economics_claims: Initial premium app: 20,000 downloads and about $8,000 in the first week (claimed)
ideas.startup_cost: Roughly $50 a month for tools plus own time (stated)
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: Search traffic took months: pages added from about March 2024 with no Google response until about August 2024

acquisition.how: SEO page generation and publishing can be agent-driven, with occasional human strategy checks.

delivery.how: AI generates the recipes and pages; occasional bug fixes needed (he notes bugs he has not looked at for months).

support.how: Low support load; a support agent can handle it.

uk_applicability.notes: A web SEO business works the same in the UK. Recipe content has some copyright and trademark sensitivity around brand names.

risks: AI-generated content and Google algorithm changes
Using restaurant brand names in recipe pages
Revenue is small and rests on a few SEO keywords
Delayed SEO feedback of about 5 months

quotes.speaker: Guest

quotes.text: it's probably revenue-wise, I think it's probably probably just doing like maybe $7, $800 a month
quotes.speaker: Guest

ideas.name: Best Dubai - city directory (restaurants, hotels, malls, schools)
ideas.one_liner: AI-generated Dubai local directory on an exact-match domain, ranking alongside Tripadvisor for restaurant review searches.
ideas.business_model: Traffic-first directory; monetisation not yet implemented (ads, affiliate or listings implied).
ideas.customer: Residents and tourists in Dubai looking for places to eat, visit and stay.
ideas.problem: Dubai's official tourism directory is basic and bloggy, with no immersive directory.
ideas.offer: Directory of restaurants, hotels, malls and schools with AI-aggregated reviews, scores, amenities, maps and FAQs, marked up with schema.

acquisition_channels.details: Schema-marked local business pages; ranks number two below Tripadvisor for 'Parker's Dubai reviews', above Facebook, Zomato, Reddit and OpenTable.

quote.text: type in like Parker's Dubai reviews, then we're number two below Trip Advisor now.
quote.speaker: Guest

ideas.delivery: Claude-generated content built on a pipeline he spent about four days researching and prompting; Webflow interface with Cursor functionality.

acquisition.how: Inbound SEO; agents can expand pages.

onboarding.how: There are no customers to onboard unless listings are sold.

delivery.how: AI aggregates reviews and content; fact accuracy checks are needed.

billing.how: No billing yet; ads or affiliate would be automated.

uk_applicability.notes: The same approach works for UK cities, but AI-aggregated Google reviews raise terms-of-service and data issues. Competition from Tripadvisor and Yelp is the same.

risks: Scraping or aggregating Google reviews may breach terms or data rules

quotes.text: zero dollars paid on advertising, costing basically nothing to build. Like when I say nothing, I mean like less than $100
quotes.speaker: Guest

ideas.offer: Product directory with comparison charts, protein-per-dollar filters, a calculator and a lead capture form.

ideas.name: Clone niche directory sites at scale
ideas.one_liner: Duplicate a vibe-coded directory project and re-skin it for many keyword niches to build many income sources.
ideas.business_model: Portfolio of SEO sites, monetised by affiliate, ads, email or sponsor placements.
ideas.customer: Searchers in each niche (toddler snacks, keto, horse feed and so on).
ideas.problem: Hosts want a repeatable, copy-paste way to run many sites.
ideas.offer: Templated directory sites across many verticals.

acquisition_channels.details: Pick keywords with KD 0-30 and high volume, with long-tail variants aggregating traffic.

ideas.delivery: Duplicate the project folder (about 10 seconds), rename it, swap pictures and branding, and regenerate content.
unit_economics_claims: First site about 3 hours, duplication about 10-15 seconds
ideas.startup_cost: Domain plus about $20 a month tools

uk_applicability.notes: Works in the UK; target UK keywords. Google may demote near-duplicate or thin sites.

tactics.name: Keyword-first niche selection with Ahrefs
steps: Use Ahrefs Keywords Explorer with a broad seed keyword
Filter for keyword difficulty 0-30
Prefer higher search volume (over 1,000 is good)
Check that long-tail variants exist and will aggregate traffic
Find the closest .com on Instant Domain Search

quote.text: you want to keyword difficulty between zero and 30
quote.speaker: Guest

tactics.name: Programmatic SEO with schema markup
steps: Create a category (for example restaurants) with Cursor/Claude and ask for schema.org properties
Generate content pages with AI
Interlink pages
Publish thousands of pages and be patient for several months

quote.text: creating content, linking between the pages of your content, you know, using schema
quote.speaker: Guest

tactics.name: Cursor writes prompts for Claude Code, with Firecrawl research
steps: Ask Cursor to research the market with Firecrawl without executing
Have Cursor write the Claude Code prompt
Paste it into Claude Code to build
Return Claude's feedback to Cursor
Make micro-iterations directly in Claude Code

quote.text: the most valuable way to use AI is to get the AI to talk to the AI
quote.speaker: Guest

tactics.name: Design inspiration folder
steps: Browse Dribbble (including /buckets) for designs
Save an image to a design reference folder in the project
Tell Claude Code to apply the style to the page

tactics.name: Clone a project to launch new niche sites
steps: Duplicate the project folder
Rename it for the new niche
Swap branding and images
Regenerate content and database data

lessons.lesson: SEO needs patience; pages can sit for months before Google rewards them, and the cost of waiting is low.

quote.text: you need to be willing to be patient, play the long game
quote.speaker: Guest

lessons.lesson: Low-price subscriptions from high-traffic pages add up, since many buyers pay and then go inactive.
Low-difficulty, high-volume keywords with a long tail of variants are the core filter for picking a niche.
Domain name matters less than structure and content for ranking, but an exact-match .com is a bonus.
Test ideas by building them rather than debating; AI cuts execution costs enough to get factual answers quickly.
Skills with AI coding tools are valuable for services as well as products; large project fees are possible.
A wrapper app may become obsolete, but building it teaches skills and momentum; many opportunities last longer than feared.

quote.text: most opportunities stick around for a while
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Large companies skip niches that are too small for them, leaving lanes for small builders.

evidence_quality.rationale: The guest is a first-hand operator with live Ahrefs data and a live build, but the revenue figures are small and unverified, the agency claims are unsupported, and the live demo is a one-shot, not a proven business. The guest's name is not given.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Guest sells 5 Day Sprint (5dayprint.com) and a Skool community; host sells the TK Owners community and has Beehiiv as a sponsor.
